title: The impact of probiotics or synbiotics on individuals with type 1 diabetes mellitus (T1DM): a systematic review and meta-analysis.
abstract: Type 1 Diabetes Mellitus (T1DM) is a chronic autoimmune condition characterized by insulin deficiency. Probiotics and synbiotics are believed to impact glycemic control. This study aims to evaluate their effects on individuals with T1DM.

title: A Lactobacillus acidophilus LA15-Bifidobacterium animalis subsp. lactis Bi66 consortium alleviates loperamide-induced constipation by coordinating gut microbiota remodeling, mucosal barrier repair, and aquaporin-mediated water transport.
abstract: Functional constipation is increasingly recognized as a microbiota-associated disorder involving impaired motility, low-grade inflammation, epithelial barrier dysfunction, and abnormal intestinal water transport. This study evaluated whether a defined probiotic consortium composed of Lactobacillus acidophilus LA15 and Bifidobacterium animalis subsp. lactis Bi66 (AB consortium; 1:1) could alleviate loperamide-induced constipation and clarified its microbiota-metabolite-barrier mechanism. title: Bifidobacterium animalis subsp. lactis BL-99 ameliorates age-related intestinal hypomotility in older adults: a randomized controlled trial.
abstract: The decay of smooth muscle contractility is a major trigger of aging-related intestinal hypomotility, which imposes a substantial healthcare burden. Despite this, effective targeted therapy for this condition remains unavailable. Here, we identified the probiotic Bifidobacterium animalis subsp. lactis BL-99 as a microbiota modulator that restores gut motility through the bile acid (BA)-mediated rescue of smooth muscle contractile function. In a randomized, double-blind clinical trial (ChiCTR2300...

title: Allobaculum stercoricanis and Its Postbiotics Alleviate Dextran Sulfate Sodium (DSS)-Induced Colitis through the Regulation of theTLR4/NF-κB Signaling Pathway.
abstract: Inflammatory bowel disease (IBD) is a chronic intestinal disorder that has become a global public health concern. Postbiotics offer advantages in biosafety and reproducibility over probiotics. Here, we demonstrated that live Allobaculum stercoricanis (A. stercoricanis) and its two postbiotic preparations─inactivated bacterial cells (POST) and cell-free fermentation supernatant (CFS)─effectively alleviated dextran sulfate sodium (DSS)-induced colitis in mice. Integrated gut microbiome and serum m...
journal: Journal of agricultural and food chemistry

title: Psychobiotics: A Paradigm Shift in Dermatological Disorders.
abstract: Recent clinical studies have demonstrated an intricate bidirectional system in the gut-brain-skin axis. Here, the gut microbiome plays dual roles: it can act as a pathological factor while also serving as a potential therapeutic target in psychodermatology. Chronic skin conditions (CSCs) like acne vulgaris, atopic dermatitis, and psoriasis are some of the leading skin problems. Besides that, these conditions are not only associated with anxiety and depression but also result in a drastic decline...

title: Transforming red lentils into a gut-friendly food: Limosilactobacillus fermentum pro-227 fermentation degrades oligosaccharides and enhances prebiotic properties.
abstract: The flatulence factors in red lentils (Lens culinaris), such as raffinose and stachyose, may limit their consumption among individuals sensitive to gastrointestinal discomfort. This study screened Limosilactobacillus fermentum pro-227, a high α-galactosidase-producing strain from the feces of healthy and long-lived elderly people to ferment red lentils (LFRL), to ferment red lentils under optimized conditions (35 °C, solid-to-liquid ratio of 1:1, inoculum level of 3%) for 24 h. title: Effects of extremely low-volume high-intensity interval training combined with iron supplementation versus iron supplementation alone on postural control in young women with iron deficiency anemia: a randomized controlled trial.
abstract: Recent research revealed postural control deterioration in young women with Iron Deficiency Anemia (IDA). To address this postural deficit, it is crucial to develop intervention strategies for postural rehabilitation in these individuals. This study aimed to explore the effect of 8-week extremely low-volume high-intensity interval training (HIIT) based on plyometric exercises combined with iron supplementation versus simple iron treatment on postural control of young women with IDA.
journal: Journal of the International Society of Sports Nutrition

title: Effects of Saccharomyces cerevisiae CNCM I-3856 and vitamin K2 on the gut microbiota of patients with osteoporosis and healthy controls using in vitro short-term colonic simulations.
abstract: The gut microbiome may be involved in bone health through the gut-bone axis. Saccharomyces cerevisiae CNCM I-3856 benefits gut health in patients with irritable bowel syndrome, which is more prevalent in women and may be associated with higher osteoporosis prevalence. We evaluated the effects of S. cerevisiae CNCM I-3856 ± vitamin K2 (K2) on the gut microbiota of patients with osteoporosis and healthy controls. Short-term in vitro colonic fermentations were performed using feces from healthy and...

title: Early post-weaning probiotic supplementation alters gut microbial community structure and predicted metabolic function in female juvenile mice.
abstract: To characterize the effects of early post-weaning multi-strain probiotic supplementation on gut microbiota composition, predicted metabolic function, and short-chain fatty acid (SCFA) profiles in female juvenile mice at the pubertal window.

title: Targeting the gut-tumor axis: probiotic therapy as an adjunct strategy in colorectal cancer treatment.
abstract: Colorectal cancer (CRC) is a multifactorial disease driven by interactions among host genetics, immune dysregulation, environmental factors, and gut microbiota. The gut-tumor axis regulates CRC progression through inflammatory signaling, oxidative stress, epithelial barrier disruption, and immune imbalance. Probiotic-derived metabolites act as bioactive molecules capable of restoring host-microbiome homeostasis and modulating tumor-associated pathways.
journal: Frontiers in cellular and infection microbiology

title: Food-Grade Metal-Phenolic Network and Polysaccharide Microencapsulation Enhances the In Vivo Anti-Colitic Efficacy of Lactiplantibacillus plantarum B112.
abstract: Probiotic therapy for inflammatory bowel disease (IBD) has a persistent practical obstacle: most cells given by mouth die before they reach the colon.

title: Effects of a Saccharomyces uvarum Cell-Based Preparation on Gut Microbial Ecology and Metabolic Activity in Adults Without Diagnosed Gastrointestinal Disease: A Randomized Placebo-Controlled Crossover Pilot Study.
abstract: Background/Objectives: Yeast-based probiotic candidates are increasingly investigated as potential modulators of gut ecology, although evidence in healthy individuals remains limited. This randomized, single-blind, crossover study primarily evaluated the tolerability of ATECREM Serius containing Saccharomyces uvarum SERIUS strain (>1010 CFU/g) and explored its effect on human gut microbiota. Methods: Forty-four volunteers completed the crossover intervention consisting of 2 months of ATECREM Ser...

title: Limosilactobacillus reuteri DSM 17938 Attenuates Hyperoxia-Induced Lung Injury in a Newborn Rat Model.
abstract: Background/Objectives: Bronchopulmonary dysplasia (BPD) remains a leading cause of morbidity in preterm infants, and effective preventive strategies are lacking. This study investigated the protective effect of orally administered Limosilactobacillus reuteri DSM 17938 in a neonatal rat model of hyperoxia-induced lung injury. Methods: Newborn Sprague-Dawley rat pups were randomly allocated to normoxia control (NC), hyperoxia control (HC), and hyperoxia with probiotic supplementation (HP) groups. ...

title: Lacticaseibacillus rhamnosus-Derived Extracellular Vesicles Alleviate Colitis via PPAR Signaling and the Gut Microbiota-Metabolite Axis.
abstract: Intestinal barrier dysfunction is a hallmark of inflammatory bowel disease (IBD), yet effective therapies remain limited, and the mechanisms of probiotic-derived extracellular vesicles (EVs) are poorly understood. Using complementary cell, murine, and intestinal organoid models, we investigated the protective effects of Lacticaseibacillus rhamnosus ZFML003-derived EVs (ZFML003-EVs). journal: Journal of agricultural and food chemistry

title: Effects of maternal Jussara (Euterpe edulis Mart.) supplementation on metabolic parameters and hypothalamic cytokine markers in male offspring at weaning following maternal trans fat intake.
abstract: Maternal consumption of trans fatty acids (TFA) during pregnancy and lactation is associated with adverse metabolic and hypothalamic cytokine-related alterations in offspring. Anthocyanin-rich fruits such as Jussara (Euterpe edulis Mart.) may counteract these effects through their antioxidant and anti-inflammatory potential. Pregnant Wistar rats (n = 24) were assigned to four diets during pregnancy and lactation: control (C), control +0.5% Jussara (CJ), trans fat-enriched (T), or trans fat + Jus...

title: Subcritical Water in Antimicrobial Benzyl Isothiocyanate Nanoemulsions Preparation and Formulation: A Novel Green Approach for Enhanced Bio-Functionality and Dietary Supplements.
abstract: Benzyl isothiocyanate (BITC) is mainly found in vegetable and fruit seeds with unique biological properties such as anti-cancer and antimicrobial properties. But BITC in pharmaceutical and food formulations faces various challenges, such as low water solubility, environmental instability, and heat sensitivity. This study developed a method based on subcritical water (SW) to prepare BITC nanoemulsion (NE) with desirable activities. Using xanthan and Arabic gums as stabilizers and Tween 80 (T 80) ...

title: Probiotic modulation of the neonatal gut-lung axis in the regulation of early respiratory function.
abstract: The gut -lung axis represents bidirectional communication between the gastrointestinal and respiratory systems that contributes to immune regulation and inflammatory homeostasis. This study evaluated the effects of probiotic-conditioned media (PCM) and live probiotics on epithelial barrier function, inflammatory responses, oxidative stress, and mitochondrial function using Caco-2 intestinal epithelial and A549 pulmonary epithelial cell models under inflammatory conditions.
journal: Frontiers in cellular and infection microbiology

title: Prophylactic administration of probiotic strains Weizmannia coagulans and Saccharomyces boulardii attenuates early dysplastic changes in an AOM/DSS-induced mouse model.
abstract: Colorectal dysplasia represents an early stage of colorectal carcinogenesis and is closely associated with chronic inflammation and altered microRNA (miRNA) expression. Probiotic strains such as Weizmannia coagulans (formerly Bacillus coagulans) and Saccharomyces boulardii possess anti-inflammatory properties and may influence host miRNA expression, suggesting their potential as prophylactic agents against inflammation-associated colorectal dysplasia.

title: The Gut Microbiota as a Mediator of the Metabolic Benefits of Fungi and Their Polysaccharides: A Review of Evidence Addressing Causality.
abstract: Prebiotic supplementation has emerged as a promising strategy to ameliorate metabolic disorders through beneficial reshaping of the gut microbiota. Accumulating evidence suggests that fungi and their polysaccharides (e.g., those from Auricularia auricula-judae, Boletus edulis, Hirsutella sinensis, Isaria cicadae, Ramaria botrytoides, and Wolfiporia cocos) possess considerable potential in this context. The present review summarizes studies providing data relevant to the potential involvement of ...

title: Heat-Inactivated Lacticaseibacillus paracasei PC-01 Alleviates DSS-Induced Colitis in Mice by Modulating Gut Microbiota and Intestinal Barrier Function.
abstract: Background: Inflammatory bowel disease (IBD) is a chronic, progressive, immune-mediated inflammatory disorder of the gastrointestinal tract. Methods: This study used C57BL/6J mice induced by DSS to construct an intestinal inflammation model, and explored the alleviating effect and potential mechanism of heat inactivated Lactobacillus paracasei PC-01 (PC-01) on intestinal inflammation. title: Dietary Selenium-Enriched Bacillus subtilis Improves Feed Utilization and Modulates Selected Responses to LPS Challenge in Laying Hens.
abstract: This study evaluated the effects of dietary selenium-enriched Bacillus subtilis (HBS) supplementation on laying performance, egg quality, and responses to lipopolysaccharide (LPS) challenge. A total of 120 Jinghong-1 laying hens received a basal or HBS-supplemented diet for 12 weeks. Subsequently, hens within each dietary replicate were allocated to phosphate-buffered saline (PBS)- or LPS-injected subgroups, and one hen per subgroup was sampled 12 h after injection, yielding six sampled hens per...

title: Heat-Inactivated Lactiplantibacillus plantarum (RSB11) as a Multifunctional Postbiotic: Anti-Inflammatory Effects Compared with Live RSB11 Across Multiple Human Cell Models.
abstract: The clinical potential of probiotics is increasingly recognized; however, dependence on microbial viability, formulation and storage constraints, and safety considerations in vulnerable populations can limit their broader application. Postbiotics offer an alternative by providing inanimate microbial preparations with retained biological activity, yet whether heat inactivation preserves the functional effects of probiotic-derived candidates remains an important question. title: Prebiotic potential and modulation of the fecal microbiota by konjac oligo-glucomannan prepared using Pediococcus acidilactici mannanase.
abstract: In this study, konjac oligo-glucomannan (KOGM) was prepared from konjac glucomannan (KGM) by enzymatic hydrolysis using β-mannanase derived from Pediococcus acidilactici HDM2. The prepared KOGM had an average molecular weight of 13.4 kDa under optimized conditions (50 °C, pH 6.0, 80 U mL-1 and 180 min). title: Cross-Cultural Adaptation and Psychometric Evaluation of the Turkish DESTEK (D-SCOPE) Questionnaire: A Multidimensional Assessment of Dietitians' Knowledge, Attitudes and Preparedness Regarding Dietary Supplements in Türkiye.
abstract: The increasing use of dietary supplements in Türkiye underscores the need for validated instruments to assess dietitians' knowledge, attitudes and self-efficacy regarding supplements. However, no validated Turkish tool is currently available. This study aimed to culturally adapt the Dietitians' Survey of Comfort, Opinions and Preparedness in Education in Supplements (-SCOPE) Questionnaire into Turkish (Diyetisyenlerin Eğitim, Supleman Tercihleri ve Konforu Anketi; DESTEK) and evaluate its psycho...
journal: Journal of human nutrition and dietetics : the official journal of the British Dietetic Association

title: Enhancement of growth, intestinal microbiota, and innate immune protection against Vibrio alginolyticus in white shrimp (Penaeus vannamei) following dietary administration with Bacillus safensis NPUST1.
abstract: Spore-forming Bacillus probiotics have attracted increasing interest as antibiotic-free functional feed additives in shrimp aquaculture. However, evidence for the probiotic potential of Bacillus safensis remains limited. This study evaluated the effects of dietary B. safensis NPUST1 on growth performance, innate immunity, intestinal microbiota, and resistance to Vibrio alginolyticus in white shrimp (Penaeus vannamei). Shrimp were fed a basal diet (control) or diets supplemented with NPUST1 at 10...

title: Microbiome-based probiotic intervention to reduce chemotherapy-induced gastrointestinal toxicity.
abstract: Chemotherapy is one of the primary treatment options for cancer; however, its gastrointestinal toxicity and disruption of gut microbial homeostasis can adversely affect patient health and treatment outcomes. This study investigated chemotherapy-induced alterations in the gut microbiome and evaluated the effects of probiotic supplementation on microbial diversity, gastrointestinal toxicity, and treatment response in cancer patients.
journal: Frontiers in cellular and infection microbiology

title: Saccharomyces boulardii reduces food intake and attenuates weight gain in diet-induced obese mice: links to gut microbial, metabolic, and immune remodeling.
abstract: The gut microbiome is a key regulator of metabolic homeostasis and contributes to obesity progression through effects on immune signaling, gut barrier integrity, and systemic inflammation. Microbiome-targeted strategies are therefore being explored as complementary approaches to conventional weight-loss therapies. Here, we investigated whether the probiotic yeast Saccharomyces boulardii modulates the gut-immune-metabolic axis in diet-induced obesity (DIO).

title: Modulation of Early-Life Calf Gut Microbiota by Bacteriocin-Producing Lactiplantibacillus pentosus AA86 and Pediococcus pentosaceus AA94.
abstract: Early-life gut microbiota plays a critical role in livestock health and productivity. Probiotic interventions, particularly those employing bacteriocin-producing lactic acid bacteria (LAB), may contribute to modulation of microbial development during this critical period. This study evaluated Lactiplantibacillus pentosus AA86 (formerly Lactobacillus pentosus) and Pediococcus pentosaceus AA94 for genomic safety, bacteriocin potential, and their effects on calf gut microbiota. Whole-genome sequenc...

title: Impact of probiotic supplementation on serum klotho levels and inflammatory status in patients with diabetic kidney disease.
abstract: Diabetic kidney disease (DKD) involves complex metabolic and inflammatory pathways, where gut dysbiosis via the gut-kidney axis plays a critical pathophysiological role. Probiotics may resolve renal decline and modulate aging biomarkers, but clinical evidence in DKD remains limited. This study evaluated the effects of Lactobacillus supplementation on serum alpha-Klotho levels, systemic inflammation, and renal biomarkers DKD patients. In an open-label, parallel-group controlled clinical trial, co...

title: Probiotic Use and Self-Reported Psychological, Cognitive, and Gastrointestinal Outcomes in a Community Sample: A Cross-Sectional Observational Study.
abstract: Research on probiotics and health outcomes has produced mixed findings. While the gut-brain axis provides a theoretical framework for probiotics to influence psychological and cognitive health, evidence remains inconsistent, particularly in community samples. This study examined associations between probiotic use and psychological, cognitive, and gastrointestinal outcomes, with particular attention to delivery method (supplement vs. fermented food).

title: Lactobacillus plantarum may prevent cholesterol gallstone formation by restoring gallbladder motility through preserving Cajal-like cells in mice.
abstract: Gallstone disease is closely linked to gallbladder dysmotility and gut microbiota dysbiosis; however, the specific role of Lactobacillus depletion in this pathogenesis remains unclear. This study investigated whether lithogenic diet (LD) induced cholesterol gallstone formation is associated with Lactobacillus deficiency and evaluated the potential of Lactobacillus plantarum (L. plantarum) supplementation to mitigate stone formation by restoring gallbladder motility.

title: Effects of dietary supplementation with the antimicrobial peptide Sublancin on growth performance, antioxidant capacity, intestinal health, immune performance, and resistance to Aeromonas hydrophila in juvenile largemouth bass (Micropterus salmoides).
abstract: A 56-day feeding trial was carried out to investigate how dietary Sublancin affects growth performance, antioxidative status, immune function, gut health, and disease resistance in largemouth bass. Five isonitrogenous and isocaloric experimental diets containing Sublancin at concentrations of 0 (Control), 100, 200, 400, and 800 mg/kg were formulated, which were respectively named Control, Sublancin 100, Sublancin 200, Sublancin 400, and Sublancin 800. Compared with the Control, the Sublancin 400...

title: Dietary baicalin supplementation increases the milk unsaturated fatty acid proportion through modulating milk metabolism and the microbiome in dairy cows.
abstract: The composition and characteristics of milk fatty acids, which play a pivotal role in nutrition, are profoundly influenced by the dietary components consumed by cows. Like other flavonoids, baicalin (BAI) may affect the proportion of milk fatty acids. This study evaluates the effect of dietary supplementation with BAI on milk microbiota and host metabolism to modulate milk fatty acid composition. Results indicated that dietary supplementation with BAI increased proportions of unsaturated fatty a...

title: Probiotics attenuate AlCl₃-induced Alzheimer's disease via gut-brain axis modulation and suppression of NF-κB/NLRP3 neuroinflammation.
abstract: Disruptions along the brain-gut-microbiota axis significantly contribute to Alzheimer's disease (AD) pathogenesis. This study evaluated the therapeutic potential of a multi-strain probiotic mixture in mitigating cognitive decline, neuroinflammation, and amyloid pathology in an AD rat model. In the present study, after induction of AD in rats by oral administration of AlCl3 (50 mg/kg) for 28 days, followed by oral treatment with a probiotic mixture (109 log CFU/ml) for 42 days. Behavioral assessm...

title: Efficacy and safety of probiotic supplementation in PsA-a randomized controlled trial.
abstract: To evaluate the clinical efficacy and safety of a multispecies probiotic in patients with PsA in moderate disease activity.

title: Modulating stress and sleep through a multi-compound dietary supplement: a randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled trial.
abstract: Stress and poor sleep are prevalent public health concerns that negatively impact well-being and daily functioning. Although adaptogens and sleep-focused supplements have separately demonstrated potential benefits, few studies have examined combined effects, particularly in healthy populations. Therefore, this study evaluated the impact of morning adaptogens, evening sleep-focused supplements, and their combination on stress, mood, and subjective and objective sleep quality.
journal: Journal of the International Society of Sports Nutrition

title: Bioprocess optimization and functional properties of cucumber juice fermented with Lacticaseibacillus casei NCDC-17: from physicochemical changes to health -promoting-effects.
abstract: A vegetable-based probiotic drink provides an alternative to dairy products for delivering beneficial microorganisms. This study was conducted to develop a fermented probiotic drink using cucumber juice. The probiotic starter culture used was Lacticaseibacillus casei NCDC-17. The fermentation process was optimized to enhance antioxidant activity, total phenolic content, and microbial viability. A rotatable central composite design using response surface methodology was used to set up the experim...

title: [Mechanisms of live combined Bifidobacterium, Lactobacillus and Enterococcus preparation in improving heat tolerance and attenuating systemic inflammatory injury in heat stroke rats].
abstract: To investigate the ameliorative effects of live combined Bifidobacterium, Lactobacillus and Enterococcus (LCBLE) preparation on heat tolerance and systemic inflammatory injury in rats with heat stroke, and to explore its underlying mechanisms.
journal: Zhejiang da xue xue bao. Yi xue ban = Journal of Zhejiang University. Medical sciences

title: Glucansucrases as versatile biocatalysts: structural insights, synthesis of emerging prebiotic oligosaccharides, and their functional roles in food matrices.
abstract: Glucansucrases (GSs), primarily members of the Glycoside Hydrolase family 70 (GH70), have emerged as transformative biocatalysts for the sustainable synthesis of high-value α-glucans and tailored oligosaccharides directly from sucrose. This review systematically explores the structural insights and catalytic mechanisms of these enzymes, emphasizing the molecular determinants of linkage specificity and domain organization. title: Probiotic Intervention With Bacillus coagulans and Lactobacillus acidophilus in Small Animals Experimental Ulcerative Colitis: Insights From a Small Animal Model.
abstract: Inflammatory bowel disease is a significant health concern not only in humans but also in companion animals and livestock, where it manifests as chronic diarrhoea, abdominal pain, and mucosal injury. Probiotics have gained increasing attention as potential therapeutic agents due to their immunomodulatory effects and ability to restore intestinal homeostasis. This study investigated the therapeutic efficacy of Bacillus coagulans and Lactobacillus acidophilus in an acetic acid-induced ulcerative c...

title: Protective Effects of Lactobacillus-Derived Probiotics and Postbiotics on Renal and Reproductive Function in Escherichia coli-Infected Rats.
abstract: Escherichia coli infections of the genitourinary tract are a major cause of renal and reproductive dysfunction in males, often impairing spermatogenesis and fertility. Probiotics and postbiotics have emerged as microbiota‑based interventions with strain‑specific immunomodulatory and antioxidant properties.

title: Generation of Probiotic-Based Multifunctional Hydrogels Capable of Carrying Oxygen and Anti-Inflammatory Drugs and Their Effect on Cell Viability Under Hypoxic Conditions.
abstract: Hypoxia and chronic inflammation have an interdependent relationship, as they stimulate each other. Under inflammation, hypoxia occurs in tissues and under hypoxia, transcription factors induce overproduction of pro-inflammatory cytokines, causing the chronic inflammatory process. There are very few studies that combine O2 with anti-inflammatory agents to simultaneously reduce the effects of hypoxia and inflammation. journal: Journal of biomedical materials research. Part A

title: Oral KCl Supplementation Safely Reduces Body Na+ Surplus and Blood Pressure.
abstract: Potassium-enriched table salt lowers blood pressure (BP) and reduces cardiovascular mortality. Whether these beneficial effects stem from reduced Na+ intake, increased K+ intake, or both is unknown. We tested the hypothesis that oral potassium chloride (KCl) supplementation lowers body Na+ content and BP in patients with essential hypertension (EH) or hyperaldosteronism, independent of salt intake.

title: Supplementation of a Bacillus-based DFM mixture on growth performance, methane emissions, microbiome, and metabolome in backgrounding beef heifers.
abstract: Direct-fed microbials (DFM) have been used to improve livestock production efficiency and reduce environmental impact. Spore-forming bacteria such as Bacillus spp. present handling and processing advantages for use as a DFM; however, more information is needed about their effects in beef cattle. The objective of this study was to evaluate the effect of a DFM composed of a mixture of B. subtilis and B. licheniformis on growth performance, nutrient utilization, enteric methane (CH4) emissions, mic...

title: A Dominant Probiotic from the Traditional Chinese Fermented Food Douzhier Exhibits Anti-Influenza Activity.
abstract: Background: Douzhier, a traditional Chinese fermented food with a history spanning over 1000 years, harbors a complex community of beneficial microbiota. In this study, we isolated Lactococcus lactis subsp. cremoris (designated L. cremoris D2022), one of the dominant bacterial species in Douzhier, and evaluated its efficacy against influenza A virus (IAV) infection. title: Effects of Curcumin Supplementation on Inflammatory Biomarkers in Adults with Type 2 Diabetes Mellitus: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis of Randomized Controlled Trials.
abstract: Background/Objectives: Chronic low-grade inflammation contributes to the pathophysiology of type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM). This systematic review and meta-analysis evaluated randomized evidence on the effects of oral curcumin or curcuminoid supplementation on circulating inflammatory biomarkers in adults with T2DM. Methods: PubMed, Scopus, and Web of Science were searched from database inception through 31 August 2026. Random-effects models using restricted maximum likelihood (REML) and Hartun...

title: Bifidobacterium animalis subsp. lactis BL-G101 Protects Against UVB-Induced Photoaging in HS68 Dermal Fibroblasts.
abstract: Background: Skin photoaging is primarily caused by prolonged ultraviolet (UV) exposure, which manifests as dryness and wrinkle formation. Recent studies highlight that beneficial microorganisms have garnered considerable attention for their emerging role in modulating host health, especially in skin photoaging. Methods: To investigate the role of two strains, Bifidobacterium animalis subsp. lactis BL-G101 (BL-G101) and Lactobacillus acidophilus LA-G80 (LA-G80), in UVB-induced photoaging, we cond...

title: Lactobacillus helveticus HY7804 Alleviates Ethanol-Induced Liver Injury and Modulates Oxidative Stress and Inflammatory Responses in a Chronic-Binge Ethanol-Fed Mouse Model.
abstract: Alcohol-associated liver disease (ALD) contributes substantially to the global burden of chronic liver disease, yet few effective pharmacological treatments are currently available. The hepatoprotective potential of Lactobacillus helveticus HY7804 was evaluated in ethanol-exposed HepG2 cells and in a modified chronic-binge ethanol-fed mouse model adapted from the National Institute on Alcohol Abuse and Alcoholism (NIAAA) paradigm. Ethanol-induced cytotoxicity in HepG2 cells was attenuated by HY7...

title: Effects of probiotic supplementation on inflammatory biomarkers in patients with depression: A systematic review and meta-analysis of randomized controlled trials.
abstract: Chronic low-grade inflammation has been widely acknowledged as an important pathophysiological mechanism underlying depression. Probiotics may alleviate depressive symptoms by modifying the microbiota-gut-brain axis and regulating inflammatory responses. The purpose of this systematic review and meta-analysis was to assess the effect of probiotic supplementation on circulating inflammatory biomarkers in depressed individuals.

title: Maternal and Embryonic Vitamin D3 Supplementation Improves Hepatic Lipid Metabolism in Progeny Chicks.
abstract: For oviparous laying hens, transition into the late-laying phase tends to be associated with reduced nutrient deposition in eggs. Accordingly, maternal dietary and in ovo supplementation of essential nutrients to eggs from late-phase hens could effectively improve embryonic development and even the subsequent performance of the offspring.
